questions.question: Which commission recommended the creation of new states on a linguistic basis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fazl Ali Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fazl Ali Commission**, formally known as the **States Reorganisation Commission (SRC)**, was established by the Government of India in **December 1953** to address demands for reorganizing states.
 
• The commission was headed by **Justice Fazl Ali** and included two other members, **H.N. Kunzru** and **K.M. Panikkar**, who examined the **linguistic**, cultural, and administrative aspects of state boundaries.
 
• In its report submitted in **September 1955**, the commission broadly accepted **language** as the basis of state reorganization, moving away from the stances of the **Dhar Commission** and **JVP Committee**.
 
• However, it rejected the rigid theory of **one language-one state**, emphasizing that the **unity of India**, administrative efficiency, and **national security** must remain primary considerations.
 
• The recommendations led to the **States Reorganisation Act, 1956**, which abolished the classification of states into Part A, B, C, and D and reorganized the country into **14 states** and **6 union territories** on **November 1, 1956**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sarkaria Commission**:

 
 
• Set up in **1983** under the chairmanship of **Justice R.S. Sarkaria** to review the working of **Centre-State relations** and suggest constitutional reforms.
 
 
 
• **Punchhi Commission**:
 
 
• Formed in **2007** under **Justice Madan Mohan Punchhi** to examine new issues in **federal relations**, including the role of the **Governor** and **inter-state cooperation**.
 
 
 
• **Rajamannar Commission**:
 
 
• Appointed by the **Tamil Nadu Government** in **1969** to study **Centre-State relations** and suggest ways to increase **state autonomy**.

questions.question: Who is the author of Maila Aanchal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phanishwar Nath Renu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Maila Aanchal**, first published in **1954**, is the most celebrated work of **Phanishwar Nath Renu** and is considered a masterpiece of modern **Hindi literature**.
 
• It is widely recognized as the first **Anchalik Upanyas** (regional novel) in Hindi, a genre that emphasizes the unique culture, local dialects, and socio-economic conditions of a specific geographical region.
 
• The novel is set in the village of **Maryganj**, located in the **Purnia district** of **Bihar**, and captures the complex social tapestry of rural India during the transition to **Independence**.
 
• The plot revolves around **Dr. Prashant**, a young physician who arrives in the village to research **malaria** and **kala-azar**, only to be drawn into the web of local **caste politics** and corruption.
 
• **Phanishwar Nath Renu** was honored with the **Padma Shri** in **1970** for his significant literary contributions, particularly for bringing **regional realism** to the forefront of Hindi fiction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Munshi Premchand**:

 
 
• Known as the **Upanyas Samrat** (Emperor of Novels), he pioneered the transition of Hindi literature into **social realism** with legendary works like **Godan**, **Gaban**, and **Nirmala**.
 
 
 
• **Yashpal**:
 
 
• A prominent **Hindi writer** and **political revolutionary** whose epic novel **Jhootha Sach** provides one of the most detailed accounts of the **Partition of India**.
 
 
 
• **Bhisham Sahni**:
 
 
• An acclaimed author and playwright best known for his novel **Tamas**, which earned him the **Sahitya Akademi Award** for its powerful depiction of the **1947 riots**.

questions.question: In which year did Pullela Gopichand win the All-England Open Badminton Championships?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2001**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pullela Gopichand** etched his name in sports history by winning the prestigious **All England Open Badminton Championships** in the year **2001**.
 
• In the final match held in **Birmingham**, he defeated the Chinese shuttler **Chen Hong** in straight sets with a score of **15-12, 15-6**.
 
• With this monumental victory, he became only the **second Indian** to claim the title, following **Prakash Padukone**, who won it in **1980**.
 
• His path to the championship was notable for a stunning victory over the then world number one, **Peter Gade** of **Denmark**, in the semi-finals.
 
• This win remains a significant milestone in **Indian badminton**, ending a 21-year drought for the nation at the world's oldest badminton tournament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prakash Padukone**:

 
 
• He was the pioneer of Indian badminton, winning the **All England** title in **1980** by defeating **Liem Swie King**.
 
 
 
• **Awards and Recognition**:
 
 
• **Pullela Gopichand** has been honored with India's highest sporting honor, the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna**, in **2001**.
 
• He received the **Arjuna Award** in **1999** and the **Dronacharya Award** in **2009** for his exceptional coaching contributions.
 
• He was also conferred with the **Padma Bhushan**, India's third-highest civilian award, in **2014**.
 
 
 
• **Legacy in Coaching**:
 
 
• Post-retirement, he established the **Pullela Gopichand Badminton Academy** in **Hyderabad**.
 
• He has mentored elite athletes including **Saina Nehwal**, **P.V. Sindhu**, and **Srikanth Kidambi**, leading them to **Olympic** and **World Championship** successes.

questions.question: The spinal cord is protected by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vertebral column**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **spinal cord** is a vital part of the **Central Nervous System (CNS)**, acting as the primary highway for **nerve impulses** traveling between the **brain** and the rest of the body.
 
• Due to its soft and delicate **nervous tissue** composition, the spinal cord requires heavy protection, which is provided by the **vertebral column** (also known as the **spine** or **backbone**).
 
• The **vertebral column** is composed of a series of bones called **vertebrae**; there are typically **33 vertebrae** in humans (some of which fuse to form the **sacrum** and **coccyx**).
 
• Each vertebra has a central opening called the **vertebral foramen**, and when stacked together, these openings form the **vertebral canal** (or spinal canal), which safely houses the **spinal cord**.
 
• This bony structure provides rigid protection against **mechanical trauma** and **impact**, while also supporting the weight of the body and allowing for **flexibility** and movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ribs**:

 
 
• These consist of **12 pairs** of curved bones that form the **thoracic cage**, primarily protecting the **heart** and **lungs** rather than the spinal cord.
 
 
 
• **Cerebellum**:
 
 
• This is a major part of the **hindbrain** located at the back of the skull, responsible for coordinating **voluntary movements**, **balance**, and **posture**.
 
 
 
• **Pons**:
 
 
• A component of the **brainstem** located above the **medulla oblongata**, it serves as a communication bridge between different parts of the brain and regulates functions like **sleep** and **respiration**.
 
 
 
• **Meninges and CSF**:
 
 
• The **spinal cord** is further shielded by three layers of membranes called **meninges** (**dura mater**, **arachnoid mater**, and **pia mater**) and is cushioned by **cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)**.

questions.question: The Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-1979) focused on:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Poverty alleviation and employment generation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fifth Five-Year Plan** was designed for the period **1974 to 1979**, with the primary objective of **Garibi Hatao** (Removal of Poverty) and the **attainment of self-reliance**.
 
• The plan placed significant emphasis on **employment generation** and social justice to reduce the gap between different economic strata of the population.
 
• The **Minimum Needs Programme (MNP)** was launched in the first year of the plan (**1974**) to provide essential services such as **rural health**, **drinking water**, **primary education**, and **nutrition** to the underprivileged.
 
• In **1975**, the **Indira Gandhi** government introduced the **Twenty Point Programme**, which focused on improving the quality of life in rural areas through land reforms and liquidation of rural indebtedness.
 
• From a statistical perspective, the plan set a **targeted growth rate** of **4.4%** per annum, and it successfully exceeded this by achieving an **actual growth rate** of **4.8%**.
 
• This plan was unique as it was terminated one year ahead of its schedule in **March 1978** by the newly elected **Janata Party** government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trade liberalization and Export-oriented growth**:

 
 
• These concepts became the cornerstone of Indian economic policy much later, specifically during the **1991 LPG (Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization)** reforms.
 
• The **Eighth Five-Year Plan (1992–1997)** was the first to fully integrate these principles to stabilize the **Balance of Payments**.
 
 
 
• **Industrialization**:
 
 
• While industry is part of every plan, **rapid industrialization** with a focus on **heavy and basic industries** was the specific hallmark of the **Second Five-Year Plan (1956–1961)**, based on the **Mahalanobis Model**.
 
 
 
• **Rolling Plan (1978–1980)**:
 
 
• Following the termination of the **Fifth Plan**, the **Janata Party** introduced the **Rolling Plan**, which involved annual assessments of economic performance rather than a fixed five-year target.

questions.question: In boxing, how many judges score an Olympic-style bout?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **Olympic-style boxing**, also known as amateur boxing, a panel consisting of **five judges** is responsible for scoring the bout to ensure a fair and transparent result.
 
• These **five judges** are positioned on all four sides of the boxing ring, which provides them with different vantage points to observe the technical execution and scoring blows of the athletes.
 
• The scoring is based on the **10-Point Must System**, which was officially adopted for Olympic competition starting from the **2016 Rio de Janeiro Games**, replacing the previous electronic punch-counting method.
 
• Under this system, the winner of each round is awarded **10 points**, while the loser receives anywhere from **7 to 9 points** based on their performance level as perceived by the panel.
 
• The use of **five judges** minimizes the risk of a single biased or incorrect scorecard determining the outcome, as the final winner is decided by the majority consensus of the panel.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Scoring Criteria**:

 
 
• Judges evaluate boxers based on the number of **quality blows** landed on the target area, **tactical superiority**, and **competitiveness** shown throughout the rounds.
 
• A **quality blow** is defined as a punch that lands with the knuckle part of the glove on the front or sides of the head or body above the belt.
 
 
 
• **Decision Types**:
 
 
• A **Unanimous Decision** is declared when all **five judges** nominate the same boxer as the winner.
 
• A **Split Decision** occurs when three judges favor one boxer while the remaining two judges favor the opponent.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Referee**:
 
 
• While the **five judges** handle the scoring, the **referee** inside the ring focuses on enforcing rules, preventing fouls, and ensuring the safety of the boxers, but does not score the fight.

questions.question: Which mineral is commonly referred to as the "key metal of industrial development"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iron**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Iron** is widely recognized as the **backbone of modern civilization** and the primary **key metal of industrial development** because it serves as the foundational material for almost all other industries.
 
• It is the essential raw material for manufacturing **industrial machinery**, **construction equipment**, and **transportation systems** like **railways**, **bridges**, and **ships**, which are vital for economic growth.
 
• The **Industrial Revolution** was fundamentally powered by the mass production of iron and its alloy, **steel**, enabling the transition from manual labor to **mechanized manufacturing**.
 
• The **per capita consumption of steel** (derived from iron) is a critical **economic indicator** used globally to measure a country's level of **industrialization** and **infrastructure maturity**.
 
• Iron ore is processed in **blast furnaces** to produce **pig iron**, which is then refined into various grades of steel suited for everything from **surgical instruments** to **heavy defense tanks**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Copper**

 
 
• Characterized by high **electrical conductivity** and **malleability**, it is primarily used in **electronics**, **telecommunications**, and **power distribution**.
 
 
 
• **Aluminum**
 
 
• Gained importance due to its **low density** and **resistance to corrosion**; it is indispensable in the **aerospace industry** and **automobile manufacturing** for reducing vehicle weight.
 
 
 
• **Manganese**
 
 
• Acts as a vital **deoxidizing agent** and alloying element; approximately **10 kg of manganese** is required to manufacture **one tonne of steel** to increase its **tensile strength** and **hardness**.

questions.question: What is the full form of NAMASTE scheme?

options.text: National Action for Mechanized Sanitation Ecosystem
New Authority for Mechanized Service Ecosystem
New Action for Mechanized Sanitation Ecosystem
National Authority for Mechanized Service Ecosystem

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Action for Mechanized Sanitation Ecosystem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **NAMASTE** scheme is a central sector initiative designed to ensure the safety, dignity, and empowerment of sanitation workers by eliminating hazardous manual cleaning practices.
 
• It is a joint venture between the **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment** (MoSJE) and the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs** (MoHUA), aiming for **zero fatalities** in sanitation work.
 
• The scheme focuses on the identification of **Sewage and Septic Tank Workers** (SSWs) across all **Urban Local Bodies** (ULBs) in India and provides them with specialized training and **Personal Protective Equipment** (PPE) kits.
 
• A core component of the project is the **mechanization** of sanitation operations, where workers are encouraged to become **sanipreneurs** by owning and operating mechanized cleaning vehicles through **capital subsidies** and interest subvention.
 
• It replaces the earlier **Self-Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers** (SRMS) to better address the modern challenges of urban sanitation infrastructure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Social Security and Health Benefits**:

 
 
• Enrolled sanitation workers and their families are provided with health insurance coverage under the **Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana** (AB-PMJAY).
 
• The scheme facilitates access to **livelihood assistance**, allowing workers to diversify their income sources and transition away from hazardous manual labor.
 
 
 
• **Institutional Framework**:
 
 
• Implementation is supported by the **National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation** (NSKFDC).
 
• Cities are mandated to set up **Sanitation Response Units** (SRU) to manage emergency cleaning requests and ensure that only trained professionals with **mechanized equipment** handle septic management.
 
• The scheme aligns with the broader goals of **Swachh Bharat Mission 2.0** to create garbage-free and water-secure cities.

questions.question: Under the AB PM-JAY expansion, senior citizens within families already covered by AB PM-JAY will receive an additional top-up cover of up to Rs ____ lakh per year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Cabinet**, chaired by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi**, approved the expansion of the **Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY)** to provide health coverage to all senior citizens aged **70 years and above**.
 
• Senior citizens belonging to families already covered under **AB PM-JAY** will receive an additional **top-up cover** of up to **Rs 5 lakh** per year.
 
• This specific **top-up cover** is meant exclusively for the senior citizen and does not have to be shared with other family members who are below the age of 70.
 
• For senior citizens aged 70 and above who are part of families not currently covered by the scheme, a cover of **Rs 5 lakh** per year will be provided on a **family basis**.
 
• Eligible senior citizens will be issued a new, **distinct card** under the **AB PM-JAY** framework to access these benefits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY**:

 
 
• Launched in **September 2018**, it is recognized as the world’s largest **publicly funded health assurance scheme**.
 
• The scheme provides a health cover of **Rs 5 lakh** per family per year for **secondary** and **tertiary care** hospitalization.
 
• It originally aimed to cover approximately **12 crore** poor and vulnerable families, representing the bottom 40% of the Indian population.
 
• Senior citizens already enrolled in other public health schemes like **CGHS**, **ECHS**, or **Ayushman CAPF** are given the choice to either continue their current scheme or migrate to **AB PM-JAY**.
 
• The expansion aims to benefit approximately **6 crore** senior citizens across **4.5 crore** households in India.

questions.question: Rudrasena II was a ruler belonging to which dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vakataka dynasty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rudrasena II** was a prominent ruler of the **Vakataka dynasty**, specifically belonging to the **Nandivardhana-Pravarapura** branch that controlled parts of the **Deccan** and **Central India**.
 
• He was the son of **Prithvisena I** and is primarily remembered for his significant **matrimonial alliance** with the **Gupta Empire**.
 
• He married **Prabhavatigupta**, the daughter of the powerful **Gupta Emperor Chandragupta II** (Vikramaditya). This alliance was a strategic move by the **Guptas** to secure their southern borders while campaigning against the **Sakas** (Western Kshatrapas).
 
• **Rudrasena II** reigned for a short period, approximately from **385 CE to 390 CE**. After his premature death, his queen **Prabhavatigupta** acted as a **regent** for their minor sons, **Divakarasena** and **Damodarasena**, effectively bringing the **Vakataka** administration under **Gupta** influence for nearly two decades.
 
• The **Vakatakas** were known as **Brahmins** and were great patrons of **Sanskrit literature** and **Brahmanical rituals**, though they also supported the development of the **Ajanta Caves**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nanda dynasty**

 
 
• Founded by **Mahapadma Nanda** in the 4th century BCE, this dynasty ruled the **Magadha** region.
 
• They were known for possessing a massive army and vast wealth, which deterred **Alexander the Great** from advancing further into India.
 
 
 
• **Maurya dynasty**
 
 
• Established by **Chandragupta Maurya** in **322 BCE** after overthrowing the **Nandas** with the assistance of **Chanakya**.
 
• It was the first empire to unify most of the Indian subcontinent, reaching its zenith under **Ashoka the Great**.
 
 
 
• **Gurjar-Pratihar dynasty**
 
 
• An imperial power that ruled much of **Northern India** from the 8th to the 11th century CE.
 
• They are celebrated for their resistance against **Arab invasions** and their involvement in the **Tripartite Struggle** for the control of **Kannauj**.

questions.question: In the context of Indian satellite launch vehicle, how many stages did the ASLV have?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Augmented Satellite Launch Vehicle (ASLV)** was a specialized project by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** designed to enhance payload capabilities to **150 kg** for **Low Earth Orbits (LEO)**.
 
• It was configured as a **five-stage** launch vehicle, utilizing **solid propellant** for all its stages to simplify the transition between experimental and operational phases.
 
• The configuration included **two identical strap-on boosters** acting as the first stage, which provided the necessary thrust to lift the **40-tonne** vehicle off the launch pad.
 
• The core of the vehicle consisted of **four successive stages**, which were largely evolved from the technologies established during the **SLV-3** program.
 
• ASLV acted as a critical technology demonstrator for **closed-loop guidance**, **bulbous heat shields**, and **vertical integration** techniques necessary for future heavy-lift vehicles.
 
• The first successful mission of the ASLV program was the **ASLV-D3**, launched on **May 20, 1992**, which successfully deployed the **SROSS-C** satellite into orbit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **SLV-3 (Satellite Launch Vehicle-3)**:

 
 
• India's first experimental launch vehicle, which was a **four-stage** all-solid propellant rocket.
 
• It successfully launched the **Rohini** satellite in **1980**, making India the sixth nation to possess satellite launch capability.
 
 
 
• **PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle)**:
 
 
• A highly reliable **four-stage** vehicle that alternates between **solid and liquid propulsion** systems.
 
• It famously utilized the **Vikas engine** for its second stage and has been the mainstay for **Sun-Synchronous Polar Orbit** missions.
 
 
 
• **GSLV (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle)**:
 
 
• A **three-stage** heavy-lift vehicle that includes a **Cryogenic Upper Stage (CUS)** powered by liquid oxygen and liquid hydrogen.

questions.question: Who became the first Indian Governor-General of independent India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**C. Rajagopalachari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chakravarti Rajagopalachari**, popularly known as **Rajaji** or **CR**, was a prominent Indian statesman, writer, and independence activist who became the **first and only Indian Governor-General** of independent India.
 
• He assumed the office of **Governor-General** on **June 21, 1948**, succeeding **Lord Mountbatten**, and served until **January 26, 1950**, when the office was abolished upon India becoming a **Republic**.
 
• During his tenure, he played a crucial role in the **constitutional transition** of India from a British Dominion to a **Sovereign Democratic Republic**.
 
• He was a leading figure in the **Indian National Congress** and was one of the first recipients of India's highest civilian award, the **Bharat Ratna**, in **1954**.
 
• Before his appointment as Governor-General, he served as the **Governor of West Bengal** and later held positions as the **Union Minister for Home Affairs** and the **Chief Minister of Madras State**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vallabh Bhai Patel**:

questions.question: There are 28 hurdle jumps and ____ water jumps in 3000 metres steeplechase event.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **3000 metres steeplechase** is a standard track and field event that requires athletes to clear a total of **35 obstacles** throughout the race.
 
• The race typically consists of an initial distance of approximately **270 metres** without any obstacles, followed by **seven complete laps** of the track.
 
• Each of these seven full laps contains **five jumps**, which are strategically placed around the 400-metre circuit.
 
• The total obstacle count is divided into **28 hurdle jumps** (dry hurdles) and **7 water jumps**, as each lap features exactly one water jump.
 
• The distribution of jumps per lap includes **four standard hurdles** and **one water jump**, usually located on the second curve of the track.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Obstacle Specifications**:

 
 
• The hurdles for the **men's** event are set at a height of **0.914 metres** (36 inches), while for the **women's** event, they are **0.762 metres** (30 inches).
 
• Unlike standard hurdles, steeplechase barriers are **solid and stationary**, designed to be stepped upon by the athletes if necessary.
 
• Each barrier must be at least **3.94 metres** wide to allow multiple runners to clear the obstacle at the same time.
 
 
 
• **Water Jump Details**:
 
 
• The **water pit** is **3.66 metres** long and **3.66 metres** wide, starting immediately after the barrier.
 
• The water depth is approximately **70 centimetres** at the barrier end and slopes upward to match the track surface level at the other end.
 
• Athletes usually step on the water jump barrier to gain leverage and leap further into the shallower part of the pit to maintain momentum.
 
 
 
• **Race Structure**:
 
 
• The order of obstacles is generally: hurdle 1, hurdle 2, hurdle 3, **water jump**, and hurdle 4 before crossing the finish line for the next lap.

questions.question: Which of the following countries is NOT in the top 5 of the Global Firepower Index 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Japan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Global Firepower Index 2025** ranks the military strength of nations based on over **60 individual factors**, including **manpower**, **equipment**, **logistics**, and **geography**.
 
• The **United States** retains its position at the top of the index with the most powerful military, followed closely by **Russia** in second place.
 
• **China** holds the **3rd** position globally, maintaining its status in the top 5 due to its massive **naval fleet** and **technological advancements**.
 
• **India** is ranked **4th** in the world, staying within the top 5 due to its significant **active personnel** and vast **land power**.
 
• **South Korea** has successfully secured the **5th** rank, largely driven by its advanced **defense industry** and high state of **military readiness**.
 
• **Japan** is currently ranked **7th** in the 2025 index, falling behind the top 5 nations despite having a highly sophisticated **Maritime Self-Defense Force**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Global Firepower Index**:

 
 
• A perfect **PowerIndex** score is 0.0000, which is realistically unattainable; the closer a country is to this score, the more powerful its military.
 
• The index does not account for **nuclear capabilities**, focusing solely on **conventional warfare** potential.
 
• It considers financial factors like **defense budget** and **purchasing power parity** (PPP) to assess sustainment capabilities.
 
 
 
• **Japan's Military Profile**:
 
 
• Japan operates under the **Article 9** of its Constitution, which limits its forces to **Self-Defense** purposes (JSDF).
 
• Despite being 7th, Japan possesses one of the most advanced **Anti-Submarine Warfare** (ASW) and **Air Defense** systems in the **Indo-Pacific** region.
